items.Sentence: Currently, all influent is first discharged into one of the ponds which serves as a treatment pond with aerators before going to the remaining evaporation/oxidation ponds.
The headworks consists of the influent pump station, bar screen, and a grit removal/classification system. The bar screen is operated as a traveling chain-and-link system that removes large solids.
Influent is pumped through a vortex grit chamber at grade.
Grit slurry collected in the vortex grit chamber is pumped to a vortex grit separator and classifier for dewatering.
Influent is pumped through a vortex grit chamber at grade.
Septage from the receiving station is passed through a coarse screen to remove large solids before proceeding to an 80-mil high density polyethylene (HDPE) lined septage holding pond.
The aerated and mixed septage holding pond will contain approximately 90,000 gallons of septage waste and have a top surface area of 4,950 square feet at freeboard.

Proposed upgrades to the treatment plant will provide secondary treatment that feeds influent from the headworks into two Biolac aeration basins... Biolac is a propriety technology using a lined basin, or pond, with a series of suspended aerators for extended aeration, activated sludge treatment. Denitrification is achieved by creating a series of oxic and anoxic zones within the basin.
The existing secondary clarifier has a 45-foot diameter and a depth of 16 feet while the new secondary clarifier will have a 65-foot diameter and a depth of 16 feet.
Denitrified, undisinfected secondary effluent will be sent to Ponds 15 and 17, which will be modified into three percolation ponds each with a depth of seven feet.
Waste sludge will be disposed into six new lined drying beds and five of the six existing lined drying beds.
Dried sludge (biosolids) are hauled offsite for disposal/reuse at an authorized reuse or disposal site.
